title: Abstract
summary: Introduction of DistilBERT and its advantages over BERT.
key_points: DistilBERT is smaller, faster, and cheaper.
source_text: we propose a method to pre-train a smaller general-purpose language representation model

title: 1 Introduction
summary: Discussion on the rise of transfer learning in NLP and the challenges of large models.
key_points: Large models improve performance but are costly.
Need for smaller models for on-device applications.
source_text: we show that it is possible to reach similar performances on many downstream-tasks

title: 2 Knowledge distillation
summary: Explanation of knowledge distillation and its application in training DistilBERT.
key_points: Distillation compresses models by training a student to mimic a teacher.
source_text: Knowledge distillation is a compression technique

title: 3 DistilBERT: a distilled version of BERT
summary: Details on the architecture and training of DistilBERT.
key_points: DistilBERT has fewer layers than BERT.
source_text: the student - DistilBERT - has the same general architecture as BERT

title: 4 Experiments
summary: Evaluation of DistilBERT on various NLP tasks and comparison with BERT.
key_points: Ablation studies highlight the importance of loss components.
source_text: We assess the language understanding and generalization capabilities of DistilBERT

title: 5 Related work
summary: Overview of related research in model distillation and compression.
key_points: Focus on task-specific distillation in prior works.
source_text: Most of the prior works focus on building task-specific distillation setups

title: 6 Conclusion and future work
summary: Summary of findings and future directions for research.
key_points: DistilBERT is a viable option for edge applications.
Further research on distillation techniques is needed.
source_text: We introduced DistilBERT, a general-purpose pre-trained version of BERT
